rows: Build spatial weights and return the neighbour graph as an edge list

rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT * FROM pysal.weights((SELECT polyid AS id, geom FROM pysal.columbus()), w_type => 'queen', id => 'id')","description":"Queen-contiguity neighbour graph for the columbus polygons"},{"sql":"SELECT * FROM pysal.weights((SELECT polyid AS id, x, y FROM pysal.columbus()), w_type => 'knn', k => 5, id => 'id')","description":"5-nearest-neighbour graph from point coordinates"},{"sql":"WITH c AS (SELECT id, crime FROM pysal.main.columbus()) SELECT w.focal::BIGINT AS id, own.crime AS crime, round(sum(w.weight * nb.crime), 2) AS neighbour_crime, count(*) AS neighbours FROM pysal.main.weights((SELECT id, geom FROM pysal.main.columbus()), w_type => 'queen', id => 'id') AS w JOIN c AS own ON own.id = w.focal::BIGINT JOIN c AS nb ON nb.id = w.neighbor::BIGINT GROUP BY w.focal, own.crime ORDER BY neighbour_crime DESC, id LIMIT 5","description":"Spatial lag of columbus crime: join the row-standardised queen weights edge list to the dataset and average each neighbourhood's neighbours' crime; the five highest-lag neighbourhoods, with their own crime and neighbour count"}]
